  1. Perma.cc

Perma.cc is an archiving website run by Harvard University. It is free to set up an account, and you get 10 webpage archives a month. Once you archive the page, you can view it as either the capture view or the screenshot view. You can then archive the Perma.cc page on archive.is or archive.fo. The only downside is that the original URL doesn't appear on archive.is.

Here is what I did with a recent Vice article.

Original URL: https://tonic.vice.com/en_us/article/59ypb8/harvey-weinstein-and-sexual-assault-trauma

Perma.cc screenshot: https://perma.cc/VZ66-NVM9?type=image

Archived version: http://archive.fo/cXjLd

  1. Snapito.com

Snapito is a screenshot website that not only captures the screenshot of a webpage, but also puts the original URL in the snapito URL. You can then archive the screenshot on archive.is. The downside to this method is that because it is only a screenshot, you can not easily search for a certain word or phrase within the text.
